name: Reputation
description: A measure of how a noble is perceived; it tells others what a noble wants, what resources he has and what he will do if provoked, and it is vital to Mythic European nobles.

name: Gratitude
description: A social currency earned by doing favors for nobles, such as delivering an enemy or hosting an exceptional feast.

name: William Marshal
description: English noble who was a child hostage of King Stephen and who later defeated the forces of Prince Louis of France in 1215.

name: John Marshal
description: William Marshal's father. He held a castle for Queen Matilda against King Stephen, broke a truce and offered his son as a hostage he would not ransom.

name: Queen Matilda
description: Rival of King Stephen for the English throne; John Marshal held a castle on her behalf.

name: King Stephen
description: King who besieged John Marshal. He threatened to catapult the hostage William but spared him instead, which changed his Reputation.

name: Mythic Europe
description: The setting of Ars Magica, a version of medieval Europe with its own nobility, Church and magic.

name: England
description: Kingdom where women have fewer rights because of the Conquest. It has earls rather than dukes, has no allods, and its covenants pay traditional fees to the king.

name: The Conquest
description: The Norman Conquest of England. It shaped English nobility, reduced women's rights and led to the counties palatine and the marcher lords.

name: Dark Secret
description: A Story Flaw. A woman who dresses as a man may carry it, and it is listed among the chivalric Story Flaws that suit knights.

name: Paid Rights
description: A free Virtue for a female character who paid a fine before play for the right to do something normally forbidden to women.

name: Story Flaw
description: A category of Flaw that draws characters into stories, such as family displeasure over Paid Rights or a female knight's unusual background.

name: Leadership
description: Ability that women raised to act as their husbands' deputies always have.

name: Profession: Steward
description: Ability that women raised to deputize for absent husbands always have, used to administer lands.

name: The Gift
description: The rare capacity for Hermetic magic. Its scarcity helped create gender equity in the Order, and magi may take Gifted children as apprentices.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The order of magi. Its Code forbids interfering with mundanes, and through Plato's influence it accepts women in all roles.

name: Plato
description: Classical philosopher who advocated training women for all duties of the state, which influenced gender equity in the Order of Hermes.

name: Margaret of Beverley
description: English pilgrim born in the Holy Land who dressed as a man to defend Jerusalem against Saladin in 1187. She later joined a nunnery at Laon.

name: Jerusalem
description: Holy city that fell to Saladin in 1187 while Margaret of Beverley helped defend it.

name: Saladin
description: Conqueror of Jerusalem in 1187.

name: Antioch
description: City where Margaret of Beverley took part in a siege.

name: Acre
description: Port from which the English army and Margaret of Beverley sailed for England.

name: Laon
description: French town whose nunnery Margaret of Beverley joined.

name: Eleanor of Aquitaine
description: Overlord of Aquitaine who went on the Second Crusade with a guard of female knights dressed as Amazons. Her conduct led to a Papal Bull forbidding women to take the cross.

name: Aquitaine
description: Region of which Eleanor was overlord.

name: Second Crusade
description: Crusade that Eleanor of Aquitaine attended with her husband.

name: Third Crusade
description: Crusade in which a Papal Bull forbade women to take the cross.

name: Sikelgaita of Sicily
description: Lombard princess and wife of the Duke of Apulia and Sicily. She fought as a knight and rallied fleeing troops at the Battle of Dyrrachium.

name: Battle of Dyrrachium
description: Battle against the Byzantine Empire in which Sikelgaita rallied fleeing troops.

name: Byzantine Empire
description: Eastern empire, now divided into successor states, that was organized into themes under strategoi.

name: Petronilla of Leicester
description: Noblewoman who armed herself as a knight in the reign of Henry II. A namesake bought from King John the right to choose her own husband.

name: Henry II
description: King of England in whose reign Petronilla of Leicester fought as a knight.

name: King John
description: King of England who fought his barons and sold Petronilla the right to choose her husband for 4000 marks.

name: Matilda of Tuscany
description: Noblewoman trained in war who championed the pope in the Investiture Controversy and nearly destroyed Imperial authority in Northern Italy.

name: Investiture Controversy
description: Conflict between pope and emperor in which Matilda of Tuscany was the pope's main supporter.

name: Church
description: The ecclesiastical institution. It gives women power through nunneries, is often opposed to tournaments and claims noble status for churchmen.

name: Nuns
description: Women who are wards of the bishop and brides of Christ. They cannot usually be forced to marry and hold much land.

name: Realms of Power: The Divine
description: Ars Magica supplement that discusses nunneries in more detail.

name: Squire
description: A young attendant to a knight, or a person qualified to be a knight who avoids the status. Also called armiger or écuyer.

name: Gentleman
description: Social Status Virtue available to squires and hidalgos.

name: Knight
description: Minor Social Status Virtue for professional mounted warriors, taken by bachelers, bannerets, hidalgos and some women.

name: Landed Noble
description: Major Virtue for a lord of the manor. It comes in Poor, standard and Wealthy versions with different manors, forces and free seasons.

name: Knight (title)
description: A professional mounted warrior (miles, chevalier), who in some places must pay his overlord a fine for dubbing others.

name: Bacheler Knight
description: A household knight in a lord's personal guard (mesnie), supported with coin and kind and led by a carissimus.

name: Protection
description: Virtue common to bachelers, bannerets and barons who are under the protection of a liege.

name: Oath of Fealty
description: Major Story Flaw for a lord who holds land from a superior in exchange for services.

name: Free Choice
description: Flaw a bacheler knight may take instead of Oath of Fealty.

name: Wealthy
description: Virtue giving extra resources. It is applied to bachelers, Landed Nobles, barons and squires.

name: Knight Banneret
description: A knight who leads other knights under his own banner. The rank can be claimed by arriving with ten liveried knights or bestowed by a liege.

name: Allod
description: Land held by descent from time immemorial rather than from a superior. Its holders need not swear fealty, and some covenants claim it.

name: Black Sheep
description: Story Flaw suited to chivalric knights.

name: Enemies
description: Story Flaw suited to chivalric knights.

name: Higher Purpose
description: Story Flaw suited to chivalric knights.

name: Heir
description: Story Flaw suited to chivalric knights.

name: True Love
description: Story Flaw suited to chivalric knights.

name: Vow
description: Story Flaw suited to chivalric knights.

name: Knightly Demands
description: Optional Major Story Flaw that replaces Oath of Fealty. The storyguide can use it to pull knights into ballad-style plots such as quests, feuds and rescues.

name: Privileged Upbringing
description: Virtue often held by children of Wealthy Landed Nobles or more senior landowners.

name: Scutage
description: A fine paid in place of knight service.

name: Great Noble
description: Virtue worth two Major Virtues, or one for supporting characters, that represents greater barons and higher ranks.

name: Baron
description: Holder of a barony (baro), divided informally into greater and lesser barons. Greater barons have the Great Noble Virtue.

name: Gentlewoman
description: Virtue for baronesses, countesses and duchesses who hold their rank by marriage.

name: Earl
description: English and Scottish equivalent of a count (comes, comte). An earl has the Great Noble Virtue and spends at least 1000 pounds a year.

name: Viscount
description: Originally a count's deputy. In France a lesser count, and in England the Latin form names sheriffs.

name: Count Palatine
description: A count with extra powers to deal with a difficult border, as in Durham and Chester.

name: Marcher Lord
description: Lords placed between England and Wales after the Conquest, with near-royal rights to build castles, levy taxes and make war.

name: Durham
description: English county palatine near the Scottish border.

name: Chester
description: English county palatine on the Welsh border.

name: Ely
description: County palatine that resisted after the Conquest, where churchmen were given extra powers.

name: Kent
description: County palatine that resisted after the Conquest.

name: Wales
description: Region bordered by the English marcher lordships.

name: Count of Marche
description: French count whose ancestor had a marcher role before southern France was pacified.

name: Duke
description: The highest class of French vassal (dux, duc), sometimes more powerful than the king. The title is not used in Britain.

name: King
description: A ruler (rex, roi) who owes allegiance to no living man except perhaps the pope or emperor. Anointed kings have minor supernatural powers and magic resistance.

name: Prince Louis of France
description: French prince offered the English crown by the barons and defeated by William Marshal.

name: Phillip Augustus
description: The current king of France, the first of his dynasty not to have his heir acclaimed while he lives.

name: King of England
description: England's monarch, who holds 15 to 20 percent of the kingdom's arable land and has 45 greater-baron vassals.

name: Magna Carta
description: Charter signed five years before 1220, when England had 197 lay and 32 ecclesiastical baronies.

name: France
description: Kingdom where the French system of titles prevails.

name: Scotland
description: Kingdom that uses the French system and the title of earl.

name: Carolingian Empire
description: The Frankish empire whose institutions underlie the French and German noble systems.

name: German System
description: System of titles in the Holy Roman Empire, marked by the prefixes reichs- (imperial) and frei- (allodial).

name: Fürst
description: German title meaning prince, in the sense of the first member of a family.

name: Prinz
description: German title for the child of a king.

name: Herr
description: German title (generosus) for any noble without a higher title, equivalent to lord.

name: Freiherr
description: German noble with an allodial holding, sometimes translated as baron.

name: Holy Roman Empire
description: The empire whose electors choose the king of the Germans, whom the pope anoints as emperor.

name: Ritter
description: General German term for a cavalry soldier, equivalent to knight.

name: Ministeriales
description: Unfree German knights who served in exchange for upkeep and are being absorbed into the hereditary knightly class.

name: Graf
description: German title equivalent to count, with variants such as burgrave and landgraf.

name: Burgrave
description: Keeper of a castle or fortified town, ranked as a viscount.

name: Landgraf
description: A graf with a larger than usual area of administration, ranked slightly above a count.

name: Margrave
description: A count with fuller legal powers over a difficult border (markgraf, marchio).

name: Brandenberg
description: Territory held by the descendants of margraves.

name: Moravia
description: Territory held by the descendants of margraves.

name: Verona
description: Territory held by the descendants of margraves.

name: Styria
description: Former march that is now a duchy.

name: Austria
description: Former march that is now a duchy.

name: Breton March
description: March in France that has since dissolved into smaller units.

name: Spanish March
description: March said to have been founded by Constantine the Great, from whose nobility Iberian nobles claim descent.

name: Constantine the Great
description: Roman emperor credited with founding the Spanish March. Some think he gave magi their role.

name: Barcelona
description: County ruled by the same family as Provence, which claims to inherit the ancient margraviate.

name: Provence
description: Region ruled with Barcelona and closely tied to Catalonian chivalry.

name: Herzog
description: German title equivalent to duke.

name: König
description: German title for king. Within the empire, kingdoms are usually held by the emperor.

name: Bohemia
description: Duchy whose duke is allowed to take the title of king.

name: Sicily
description: Kingdom held personally by the emperor. It is his center of power and has small, poor counties.

name: Römischer Kaiser
description: Roman Emperor, a title granted in the West through election by the electors of the Holy Roman Empire and anointing by the pope.

name: Frederick II
description: Holy Roman Emperor elect, anointed on 22 November 1220 and centered in Sicily. His court welcomes Muslim and Christian scholars and he has some interest in magic.

name: Pope
description: Head of the Church, who anoints the emperor and recognizes kings. He has Magic Resistance 25.

name: Reconquista
description: The Christian conquest of Muslim Iberia, which shaped Iberian noble and town systems.

name: Iberia
description: Peninsula of the Christian kingdoms, with the fuero-based noble system.

name: Fuero
description: Iberian town charter that sets out militia obligations, exemptions and the equipment required of caballeros.

name: Peon
description: Iberian townsman who fights on foot.

name: Infanzone
description: The lowest rank of Iberian gentry.

name: Caballero
description: Iberian mounted warrior whose status depends on keeping his gear and serving in the field.

name: Castile
description: Iberian kingdom where a bride might keep ruling her own lands and widows may act as guardians.

name: Portugal
description: Kingdom where some archers hold caballero status.

name: Catalonia
description: Iberian region whose chivalry follows the French model, with condes, viscondes, valvasores, cavallers and sotcastlàs.

name: Valvasore
description: Catalan noble with a retinue of five knights, similar to a banneret.

name: Caballer
description: Catalan vassal who rules a single castle.

name: Sotcastlà
description: Catalan vassal holding a fief that supports one knight.

name: Caballero Villano
description: Caballero tied to a particular town who must live there and be ready to muster.

name: Dependents
description: Flaw that ties a caballero villano to his town through his family.

name: Knightly Duties
description: Flaw a caballero villano may take instead of Dependents.

name: Hidalgo
description: Ancestral caballero backed by his family in matters of honor, with the Knight Virtue.

name: Ricohombre
description: Iberian great men of the aristocratic upper class who hold honores from kings. They have the Great Noble Virtue.

name: Visigothic kings
description: Ancient kings from whom ricohombres claim descent.

name: Italy
description: Region where nobility is simple, counts are weak and communes govern the towns.

name: Papal States
description: Territory in Italy outside the communes' control.

name: Patrizio
description: Patrician of a northern Italian town's ruling elite, ranked above squire and below knight.

name: Venice
description: City where patricians descend from the founders listed in the Golden Book and sit on the Council.

name: Golden Book
description: Venetian register of the city's founding families.

name: Strategos
description: Byzantine general who controls a theme.

name: Despot
description: Leader of a Byzantine successor state who grants pronia.

name: Pronia
description: Byzantine grants of land revenues in exchange for military support.

name: Constantinople
description: Byzantine capital whose fall divided the empire.

name: Latin Empire
description: Crusader state in the former Byzantine lands that uses the French structure.

name: Code of Hermes
description: The Order's law, which strictly forbids interfering with mundanes and molesting faeries.

name: Interference
description: Meddling with mundanes that brings ruin on the Order, forbidden by the Code. Its definition varies by Tribunal.

name: Tribunal
description: Regional Hermetic assembly that judges crimes and regulates interference and the sale of magic items.

name: Covenant
description: A community of magi, which may dwell on allods or must deal with mundane neighbors.

name: Conspiracy
description: Allying with mundanes in common cause, which the Code forbids. Aid given without the recipient's knowledge is not conspiracy.

name: Lord Cuthbert
description: Example noble feuding with a magus.

name: Sir Dudley
description: Example enemy of Lord Cuthbert.

name: House Mercere
description: Hermetic House of messengers who carry created goods to distant markets. Some of its covenants tie their finances to cities.

name: Alps
description: Tribunal with the strictest rules on interference.

name: Normandy
description: Tribunal where covenants keep a mundane veneer, so that interference means only harm to other magi.

name: Rhine
description: Tribunal where most covenants claim to be allodial and refuse to pay taxes.

name: Longevity Potion
description: Magical potion given to a covenant's tame noble in exchange for service.

name: Magic Items
description: Enchanted devices whose sale to nobles has been forbidden since 1061, although a loophole allows sale through mundane servants.

name: Infernal
description: Realm of demons, whose auras famine could feed.

name: House Verditius
description: Hermetic House whose current primus wants freer access to mortal markets for magic items.

name: Grand Tribunal
description: Order-wide Tribunal that could be asked to restrict the sale of magic items.

name: Involvement
description: Contact with mundanes that does not breach the Code, such as proportionate self-defense.

name: Self-Defense
description: The right of magi to defend themselves, broadly defined.

name: Defense of Sodales
description: The right of magi to act in a fellow magus's defense, for example by rescuing prisoners or avenging Redcaps.

name: Defense of the Art
description: The right to treat as an enemy anyone who publicly vows to purge wizards.

name: Redcap
description: Messengers of the Order, who wear red caps and whose harm is avenged.

name: Waiting Spell
description: Spell that killed a raiding noble when his specific presence triggered it.

name: Schism War
description: The Order's past war, when some magi turned to Satan, during which purge declarations were common.

name: Magic Theory
description: Hermetic Ability of which a stolen apprentice knows only a smattering.

name: Direction Sense
description: Minor magical talent a Redcap's apprentice might show.

name: Dowsing
description: Minor magical talent a Redcap's apprentice might show.

name: Vis
description: Raw magical power. Magi collect it from sites and defend vis sources.

name: Order of Hermes Lore
description: Knowledge of the Order, in which educated nobles may have low scores.

name: House Jerbiton
description: Hermetic House tied to nobles and cities. It spreads misconceptions about magi and administers the plea.

name: Hedge Wizard
description: Non-Hermetic magician, such as the hedge witches and wise women purged by a baron.

name: Plea
description: The means by which noblemen raise legal issues with the Order, administered by redcaps, Guernicus or Jerbiton.

name: House Guernicus
description: Hermetic House that helps administer nobles' pleas.

name: Magic Resistance
description: Protection that church officers and anointed sovereigns get against magic, from the pope's 25 to a crowned king's 10.

name: Aura of Rightful Authority
description: Penetration 0 effect held by church officers and sovereigns out to Voice range.

name: Cardinal
description: Church officer with Magic Resistance 20.

name: Archbishop
description: Church officer with Magic Resistance 10.

name: Relics
description: Saints' relics, which grant Magic Resistance.

name: Demonstrating Harm
description: The part of a plea in which harm to a magus's interests must be shown.

name: House Flambeau
description: Hermetic House known for fire magic.

name: Thirteenth House
description: House destroyed for paganism or Satanism.

name: King Arthur
description: Legendary king whom some believe gave magi their role, and the theme of Arthurian feasts.

name: Charlemagne
description: Emperor whom some believe gave magi their role.

name: Divine
description: The highest Realm. Its Dominion suppresses magic and it judges diabolists.

name: Dominion
description: The Divine aura that suppresses magic in cities and holy places.

name: Quaesitores
description: Hermetic investigators who examine covenants destroyed by acts of God.

name: Corruption of House Tytalus
description: The fall of House Tytalus, in which God did not intervene directly.

name: House Tytalus
description: Hermetic House that suffered a Corruption.

name: Demon
description: Infernal beings such as demons of pride, famine and avarice that oppose reform or exploit it.

name: Famine Demons
description: Demons that attack a covenant that creates bountiful crops.

name: Demon of Avarice
description: Demon that aids magi hoping to create a merchant class whose souls he can claim.

name: Faerie
description: Beings that force humans to act out stories and so preserve conservative social roles.

name: Arcadia
description: Realm of faeries where ancient powerful faeries may dwell.

name: Faerie Ancestor Spirit
description: Powerful faerie that kidnaps a child to pose as a false heir.

name: Magical Animal Companions
description: Magical animals for which the pet statistics can serve as templates.

name: Magpie
description: Talking pet bird with game statistics.

name: Monkey
description: Pet with game statistics.

name: Squirrel
description: Pet with game statistics.

name: Lightning Reflexes
description: Virtue possessed by the squirrel.

name: Athletics
description: Ability used for dance performance and animal movement.

name: Awareness
description: Ability of animals.

name: Brawl
description: Ability of animals.

name: Music
description: Ability, such as the magpie's mimicry.

name: Stealth
description: Ability of animals.

name: Survival
description: Ability of animals.

name: Chess
description: Board game valued for teaching military strategy.

name: Tafl
description: Popular Norse board game of defending a king.

name: Fidchell
description: Celtic protect-the-king board game.

name: Rithmomachia
description: The philosopher's game.

name: Carouse
description: Ability used for games of chance and companionship.

name: Etiquette
description: Ability used for good manners, seating guests and court dance.

name: Octavian of Tremere
description: Tremere magus who plays chess with a great noble and may be breaking the Code.

name: House Tremere
description: Hermetic House of Octavian.

name: Coeris Gambit
description: Chess move of Octavian.

name: Hazard
description: Dice game.

name: Luck
description: Virtue providing bonus to die rolls.

name: Legerdemain
description: Ability to manipulate dice and cheat.

name: Concentration
description: Ability for games of skill.

name: Perception
description: Characteristic combined with Carouse.

name: Carol
description: Circle dance.

name: Estampie
description: Stamping dance.

name: Salterello
description: Leaping dance from Naples.

name: Area Lore
description: Ability for local folk dances.

name: Damsel's Tresses
description: Rare golden spice growing on an ancient oak.

name: Feast of St. John
description: Holiday of a feast story.

name: Aura
description: Supernatural auras, such as Infernal auras.

name: Hunting
description: Noble sport.

name: Chase
description: Reserved hunting ground; Minor Surroundings Boon.
